topStories.headline: Shovels Are Finally in the Ground at 400 Divisadero — A Decade of Delays Is Over
topStories.dek: Greystar began construction work at the former Touchless Car Wash site this fall, breaking a ten-year logjam that made the empty lot a citywide symbol of stalled housing.
topStories.body:
After more than a decade of aborted plans, changing building codes, and rotating developers, construction activity has started at 400 Divisadero Street, the corner lot at Oak that was home to the shuttered Touchless Car Wash. Greystar, the largest apartment developer in the United States, acquired the site from prior developer 4Terra Investments, secured financing, and obtained Public Works permits listing an October 19 start date for sidewalk and street closures along the Divisadero and Oak frontages.

The project calls for an eight-story, 203-unit mixed-use building with approximately 1,850 square feet of ground-floor retail, parking for 24 cars and 144 bicycles, and 20 deed-restricted affordable apartments. The structure will rise 85 feet and produce roughly 194,000 square feet of building area, with a mix of one- and two-bedroom units designed for the NoPa and Lower Haight market.

District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who made reviving the project a campaign centerpiece when he defeated Dean Preston in 2024, worked with the Mayor's Office and the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development to reduce impact fees and pass legislation locking building-code compliance to the date of permit application — a change that reportedly saved the project millions in construction costs. The building-code version had shifted three times over the project's lifespan, adding an estimated 5 to 7 percent to costs.

The development will be the largest housing project along the Divisadero corridor and is expected to be the first significant market-rate apartment building to begin construction in San Francisco in 2026. Critics, including the Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council, have questioned Greystar's record as a corporate landlord, pointing to federal antitrust investigations and tenant complaints across its national portfolio. Those concerns have so far not halted the project. Completion is not expected until 2028 at the earliest.

topStories.headline: TEDxHayesValley Launches Its First-Ever Salon Event This Saturday
topStories.dek: The brand-new TEDxHayesValley organization hosts a free afternoon salon at Unity San Francisco on November 14, offering a preview of the full conference planned for February 2027.
topStories.body:
Hayes Valley is getting its own TED chapter, and next Saturday is the first chance to see what it looks like. TEDxHayesValley is hosting a free Salon event on Saturday, November 14, from 2 to 5 p.m. at Unity San Francisco, 240 Page Street. The gathering is billed as an introductory afternoon of curated TED Talks, conversation, and community-building ahead of the full TEDxHayesValley conference scheduled for February 6, 2027, at the same venue.

The salon is free to attend, though organizers are asking guests to RSVP in advance via the TEDxHayesValley website. Applications to speak at the February conference are also open. The event reflects a broader surge of civic programming in the neighborhood, which has also seen the launch of the Hayes Valley Entertainment Zone, a new weekly farmers' market, and regular Head West Marketplace pop-ups at Patricia's Green this year.

topStories.headline: Hayes Valley's To-Go Drink Zone Has Four Weeks Left — Then It Hibernates for Winter
topStories.dek: The Hayes Valley Entertainment Zone, which lets patrons carry cocktails, beer, and wine on the street from participating bars and restaurants, runs only through November 28.
topStories.body:
Residents and visitors have been able to stroll Hayes Street with a to-go drink in hand since late July, when the Hayes Valley Merchants Council, the Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association, and Hayes Promenade jointly launched the neighborhood's first Entertainment Zone. The EZ — a city-designated area where to-go alcoholic beverages from licensed businesses are permitted on public sidewalks — has been active every Friday from 4 to 10 p.m. and every Saturday from noon to 10 p.m.

The current run ends Saturday, November 28, according to the Hayes Promenade events calendar. Participating bars and restaurants rotate week to week; the Hayes Promenade website publishes a current list each week. The EZ was modeled on similar zones in other San Francisco neighborhoods and was soft-launched alongside the Hayes Valley Carnival earlier this summer. Whether the program will return in 2027 has not yet been announced.

events.title: Hayes Valley Farmers' Market
events.description: The Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association brings Bay Area growers and local vendors to Hayes Street every Saturday. Note that Hayes Street is closed to cars on market days, and the Muni 6 Hayes/Parnassus route is rerouted.

events.title: Hayes Valley Entertainment Zone
events.description: Participating bars and restaurants along Hayes Street are licensed to sell to-go cocktails, beer, and wine for sidewalk consumption through the final Saturday of November. Check the Hayes Promenade website for the current weekly roster of participants.

moreNews.headline: Hayes Street Closed to Cars Every Friday and Saturday This Month
moreNews.body: SFMTA has formalized the Hayes Street closure schedule for November 2026: the block between Gough and Octavia is car-free every Friday evening and all day Saturday for the Hayes Valley Farmers' Market and Shared Spaces programming. The Muni 6 Hayes/Parnassus route is rerouted around the closure during those windows, with temporary flag stops on Grove Street at Gough and Laguna. The closure pattern is expected to continue through the end of 2026, according to SFMTA's November advisory published November 3.

moreNews.headline: 650 Divisadero Affordable Project Enters Construction Window
moreNews.body: The 107-unit all-affordable apartment building planned for the corner of Divisadero and Grove Streets — one block from Alamo Square and next door to The Independent music venue — was scheduled to begin construction in late 2026, according to developer filings with the city. The ten-story project is sponsored jointly by Young Community Developers and Jonathan Rose Companies in partnership with the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development, which has committed $21.25 million to the development. Mithun is the architect of record. Units are not expected to be ready for occupancy until 2028.

restaurants.name: Rich Table
restaurants.description: Husband-and-wife chefs Evan and Sarah Rich serve hyper-seasonal, inventive California cuisine in a lively Hayes Valley dining room — one of SF's toughest reservations since 2012.

restaurants.name: RT Bistro
restaurants.description: The more casual, 37-seat sister spot to Rich Table — opened early 2026 next door — featuring the RT Bistro burger, one-layer lasagna, and a crowd-pleasing bistro menu.

restaurants.name: RT Rotisserie
restaurants.description: The Rich Table team's fast-casual offshoot focused on rotisserie chicken and home-style seasonal dishes, open daily in Hayes Valley.

restaurants.name: Nightbird
restaurants.description: Chef Kim Alter's intimate, Michelin-recognized Hayes Valley restaurant offers a seasonal tasting menu behind a carved-owl wooden door on Gough Street.

restaurants.name: Absinthe Brasserie & Bar
restaurants.description: A Hayes Valley institution since 1998, serving upscale French brasserie fare and craft cocktails in a Belle Époque-inspired room steps from SF's performing arts venues.

restaurants.name: Zuni Café
restaurants.description: A San Francisco institution since 1979, Zuni occupies a triangular Market Street building and is legendary for its wood-fired roast chicken and brick-oven cooking.

restaurants.name: Suppenküche
restaurants.description: Hayes Valley's beloved Bavarian Wirthaus since 1993, offering hearty German classics like schnitzel, pretzels, and an exceptional specialty beer list.

restaurants.name: Dumpling Home
restaurants.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand-recognized Hayes Valley spot serving hand-folded xiao long bao (soup dumplings), pan-fried buns, and other Chinese classics.

restaurants.name: Hazie's
restaurants.description: A stylish Hayes Valley restaurant praised for its cocktails, happy hour, and modern American dinner menu in a comfortable neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Souvla
restaurants.description: The original Hayes Valley location of this beloved Greek fast-casual chain, known for rotisserie meats, big salads, and a sunny backyard patio.

restaurants.name: Chez Maman West
restaurants.description: A cozy Hayes Valley French bistro serving classics like steak frites, mussels, and crêpes in a lively street-side setting.

restaurants.name: Smuggler's Cove
restaurants.description: A three-story Hayes Valley tiki bar with more than 1,300 varieties of rum — the largest selection of any bar in the US — and a 80-cocktail menu of tiki classics and originals.

restaurants.name: Nopa
restaurants.description: The neighborhood namesake at 560 Divisadero has served organic wood-fired California cuisine with a daily-changing menu since 2006, remaining one of SF's most beloved dining rooms.

restaurants.name: Bar Crudo
restaurants.description: A vibrant NoPa raw bar specializing in creative crudo, fresh oysters, and sustainably sourced seafood, with a popular happy hour running Monday through Saturday.

restaurants.name: Horsefeather
restaurants.type: Cocktail bar and New American restaurant
restaurants.description: A reliably good NoPa cocktail bar and restaurant with inventive drinks, fried chicken, duck fat fries, and a warm Arts-and-Crafts-inspired interior open late nightly.

restaurants.name: Brenda's Meat & Three
restaurants.description: New Orleans–born chef Brenda Buenviaje's NoPa diner lets diners choose one meat and three sides from a rotating array of down-home Southern classics, with a legendary breakfast menu.

restaurants.name: Nopalito
restaurants.description: Chef Gonzalo Guzmán's original Broderick Street location — open since 2009 — serving blue-corn tacos, carnitas, and seasonal Mexican dishes rooted in Veracruz family cooking.

restaurants.name: Altamirano Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: A spacious NoPa Peruvian restaurant with an exhibition kitchen, a lively bar, and an outdoor courtyard with a fire pit for dining al fresco.

hotels.name: Hayes Valley Inn
hotels.description: A well-located, affordable 2-star inn on Gough Street in the heart of Hayes Valley, offering easy access to the neighborhood's restaurants, shops, and performing arts venues.

hotels.name: The Grove Inn
hotels.description: A family-owned Italianate-Victorian style inn in the heart of the Alamo Square Historic District, operating for over four decades and continuing a legacy dating to 1865.

hotels.name: Symphony Inn
hotels.description: A well-maintained budget motel in Hayes Valley, conveniently located near City Hall and the performing arts district with easy access to neighborhood restaurants.

hotels.name: Inn at the Opera
hotels.description: An intimate boutique hotel ideally located in the Performing Arts District near Hayes Valley, catering to opera, symphony, and ballet patrons.

hotels.name: Casa Loma Hotel
hotels.description: A European-style budget hotel near Hayes Valley offering affordable accommodation with easy access to public transit and the neighborhood's dining scene.

shops.name: MAC (Modern Appealing Clothing)
shops.description: A long-running Hayes Valley fixture carrying local and independent labels — including Dries Van Noten and Junya Watanabe — curated by owners with encyclopedic knowledge of upscale, quirky fashion.

shops.name: Métier
shops.description: An intimate Hayes Valley jewelry salon specializing in one-of-a-kind estate and contemporary pieces by artists including Gabriella Kiss, Harwell Godfrey, and Gillian Conroy.

shops.name: AETHER Apparel
shops.description: A striking Hayes Valley store built from three stacked shipping containers, carrying the brand's full line of technical outerwear and travel-ready layers.

shops.name: Cotton Sheep
shops.description: A family-run Hayes Valley boutique specializing in rare Japanese denim labels like Kapital, jewelry from Masato, crafted bags from Porter, and curated home goods.

shops.name: Marine Layer
shops.description: Hayes Valley outpost of the popular SF-founded brand, offering signature soft knits, sweatshirts, and tees made from cotton-modal blends.

shops.name: Peak Design
shops.type: Camera and travel gear flagship store
shops.description: The flagship Hayes Valley store for the SF-based Peak Design, selling bags, camera straps, tripods, and everyday carry gear in a beautifully designed retail space.

shops.name: The Epicurean Trader
shops.description: A curated Hayes Valley shop stocking artisan provisions, craft beer, wine, and spirits alongside an in-house coffee bar.

shops.name: Fiddlesticks
shops.description: A cheerful Hayes Street children's boutique stocked with colorful clothing, toys, and books, blending playful design with durable quality.

shops.name: Bulo Shoes
shops.description: A well-regarded Hayes Street shoe boutique carrying a carefully edited selection of European and independent footwear brands.

shops.name: minimal
shops.description: A carefully curated Hayes Valley shop offering Scandinavian-inspired rugs, furniture, lighting, ceramics, and textiles including a large selection of sustainable Swedish rugs.
shops.address: 450 Hayes St C-1, San Francisco, CA 94102

shops.name: Azil Boutique
shops.description: A charming Hayes Valley boutique known for its distinctive jewelry selection and dainty accessories at accessible price points.

shops.name: Todd Snyder
shops.description: The Hayes Valley outpost of the upscale American menswear brand, offering curated clothing, footwear, in-house tailoring, and private appointments.

artEntertainment.name: SFJAZZ Center
artEntertainment.type: Jazz and world music concert hall
artEntertainment.description: The first stand-alone structure in the US built specifically for jazz, SFJAZZ presents more than 100 concerts a year in the Robert N. Miner Auditorium and the 100-seat Joe Henderson Lab at the corner of Franklin and Fell streets.

artEntertainment.name: Orpheum Theatre
artEntertainment.description: A 2,197-seat San Francisco landmark theater dating to 1926, operated by ATG Entertainment (BroadwaySF), hosting major Broadway touring productions on Market Street.

artEntertainment.name: Haight Street Art Center
artEntertainment.type: Nonprofit poster art gallery and printmaking studio
artEntertainment.description: Opened in 2017, this nonprofit gallery and printmaking studio at 215 Haight Street celebrates the history and cultural impact of poster art, with free rotating exhibitions open Thursday–Sunday.

artEntertainment.name: Hayes Valley Art Works
artEntertainment.description: A converted shipping-container gallery at Oak and Octavia operated by the Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association, hosting exhibitions, monthly Jazz Jams, weekend workshops, and a community garden.

artEntertainment.name: Alamo Square Park
artEntertainment.description: The iconic hilltop park famous for the "Painted Ladies" Victorian row houses along Steiner Street, offering panoramic views of the San Francisco skyline and a beloved gathering space for locals.
artEntertainment.address: Hayes St & Steiner St, San Francisco, CA 94117

artEntertainment.name: Madrone Art Bar
artEntertainment.type: Art bar and live music venue
artEntertainment.description: A distinctive Divisadero bar where local artists display work on the walls, friendly neighborhood clientele mingles amid eclectic décor, and live music fills the room on select nights.

artEntertainment.name: Patricia's Green
artEntertainment.description: The social heart of Hayes Valley: a pocket park on Octavia Boulevard featuring rotating Burning Man–inspired sculpture installations and picnic space created after the Central Freeway was removed.
artEntertainment.address: Octavia Blvd & Hayes St, San Francisco, CA 94102

gymsRecreation.name: Folk Yoga NoPa
gymsRecreation.description: One of San Francisco's oldest locally-owned yoga studios — operating since 1998 — in a charming Victorian on Divisadero Street, offering hot, power, prenatal, restorative, and yin yoga classes.

gymsRecreation.name: Live Fit Gym – Hayes Valley
gymsRecreation.description: A family-owned, highly rated Hayes Valley gym on Octavia Street offering personalized training, chiropractic, massage, and small-group fitness classes.

gymsRecreation.name: Perform For Life SF
gymsRecreation.description: A top-rated Hayes Valley studio offering group fitness classes, personal training, and performance coaching in a supportive, community-focused environment.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga – NoPa
gymsRecreation.description: A modern heated studio on Divisadero Street offering hot yoga, yoga sculpt, power vinyasa, functional strength training, and restorative recovery classes for all levels.

gymsRecreation.name: Club Pilates – NoPa
gymsRecreation.description: A NoPa reformer-based Pilates studio on Fulton Street offering full-body group workout classes designed to increase mobility, balance, and strength.

gymsRecreation.name: LuxFit – Hayes Valley
gymsRecreation.description: A premier outdoor gym on Octavia Street in Hayes Valley offering personal training, small-group outdoor workouts, and open gym memberships.

gymsRecreation.name: FITNESS SF – Fillmore
gymsRecreation.description: A well-priced, full-service gym in the Western Addition open until midnight on most nights, offering cardio equipment, free weights, and group fitness classes.

gymsRecreation.name: Panhandle Park
gymsRecreation.description: The long, tree-lined Panhandle strip connecting the NoPa neighborhood to Golden Gate Park is a beloved outdoor space for running, cycling, dog-walking, and informal recreation.
gymsRecreation.address: Fell St & Stanyan St, San Francisco, CA 94117
